Subject: Hosted API: annualize throughput lane & billing limiter

Hi Jill and Arjun,

Thanks again for the productive call last week — great to see Acme continuing to expand the personalization use cases. Based on the growth signals you shared, I put together a short proposal to annualize the hosted API commit and introduce a billing limiter (safeguard) so you get predictable pricing and we avoid surprise overages during holiday spikes.

Proposal (high-level):
- Monthly committed throughput: move from 1.2B tokens/mo to 2.0B tokens/mo (annualized cadence, invoiced monthly).
- New tier mapping: shift to Tier 3 pricing band (reduced per-token rate for committed usage).
- Billing limiter: soft cap at +15% burst above commit; soft-overage invoiced at discounted overage rate with automated alerts and a configurable hard cap option.
- Ops: 30-day staged rollout — shadow traffic, prefix cache warm-up, then full roll on day 31.

Next steps I suggest: legal/finance sign-off on the amendment, ops runbook with Karthik for rollout, and procurement PO for the first invoice. I attached a draft amendment and a short ops checklist we can use as a starting point.

Are you available Wednesday for a 30-minute alignment to lock cadence and any SLA exceptions?

Thanks,
Steph

Hi all — adding a quick ops perspective and recommended thresholds.

Technical roll plan (30-day staged):
- Days 0–7: Shadow traffic at 25% of projected increase (no billable deviation), warm KV cache for common prefixes.
- Days 8–21: Gradual shift to 60% throughput increase for non-critical routes; monitor p95 latency and token egress.
- Days 22–30: Full traffic on upgraded commit.

Rollback and safety thresholds (recommended):
- p95 latency threshold: 250ms for inference endpoints (if exceeded for >15 minutes, auto-shift 20% traffic back to previous commit).
- Error rate threshold: >0.8% request error rate for 10 minutes triggers immediate rollback and pager to Redwood on-call.
- Cost guard: soft cap alerts at 85% of monthly commit and hard invoice stop if you enable the hard cap at +5% over commit (only enabled if Acme opts in).

Overage pricing options (examples):
- Soft-overage (between commit and +15%): $0.0028 per 1K tokens (discounted vs pay-as-you-go).
- Hard cap opt-in overage (if enabled): billing halts and requests queue until Acme authorizes release or sets new cap.

I’ll prepare the ops_playbook spreadsheet with links to dashboards and alert runbooks; attaching a stub. Happy to walk through this Wed 10:00am PT.

—Karthik
